title: Elements, Atoms and Compounds
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Elements, Atoms and Compounds Worksheets (Symbols and Formulae)
standard_code: KS3 Chemistry: Atoms, elements and compounds
standard_text: A simple (Dalton) atomic model; differences between atoms, elements and compounds; chemical symbols and formulae for elements and compounds; conservation of mass changes of state and chemical reactions.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on elements, atoms and compounds: chemical symbols, formulae, counting atoms, naming compounds and telling elements, compounds and mixtures apart. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements have one type of atom.
key_sub: Compounds have different atoms chemically joined; H₂O has 2 H and 1 O.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of atoms.

  • An element has only one type of atom. A compound has different atoms chemically joined.
  • Each element has a symbol (O, Fe, Na). A formula shows the atoms in a compound: H₂O has 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen.
  • A mixture contains substances that are not chemically joined.
Example

Atoms in CH₄?

1 C + 4 H

Answer: 5

Example

Symbol for iron?

From the Latin ferrum

Answer: Fe

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water is an element.
  • Thinking air is a compound.
  • Thinking a compound is just a mixture of elements.

faq.q: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
faq.a: An element contains only one type of atom, like oxygen or iron. A compound contains two or more different atoms chemically joined, like water (H₂O).

faq.q: How do you read a chemical formula?
faq.a: Each symbol is an element, and the small number after it tells you how many of those atoms there are. CO₂ has one carbon and two oxygen atoms.
No. Air is a mixture of gases (mainly nitrogen and oxygen) that are not chemically joined.
